properties.name: find_tools ranked plan_epoch for a query about what HAPPENED, because its description contains "has NOT happened" — and add_epoch did not appear at all
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-10, after Anthony asked whether this session was using reflow2 at all or discovering its behaviour some other way. It was not using reflow2. Every behavioural fact reported across a day of work came from READING RUST: `record_change` refusing history into a planned epoch (temporal.rs), the brainstorm exemption (heal.rs), the prescribed layer pairs (capture.rs), seam_coverage counting existence rather than content (maturity.rs), the unwritable `created_at` (grep over schema/temporal.yaml against the toolsnap JSON). `find_tools` was not called once.

THE TEST, run in his own terms — ask it the question a USER would ask, in their words. Query: "record when a point in time actually happened so changes pinned to it can be ordered by date".

  1  relation_candidates    unrelated
  2  invalidates            unrelated
  3  set_evidence_scope     unrelated
  4  invalidated_findings   unrelated
  5  plan_epoch             THE OPPOSITE TOOL — it creates a point that has NOT happened

`add_epoch`, the correct answer, did not appear in the top five of 180 searched. And the reason `plan_epoch` ranked is legible: its description reads "an Epoch that has NOT happened yet", the query said "happened", and a bag-of-words match scored the negation as a hit.

⭐ THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS IN ONE DAY, and that is what makes it structural rather than a bad query. (a) `settled_question_prose`'s markers cannot tell a node ASSERTING a question is open from one QUOTING an old one. (b) The test written for it blacklisted substrings and failed on its own note's disclaimer, "nothing here CLAIMS THE TEXT IS WRONG". (c) This. A LEXICAL INSTRUMENT CANNOT DISTINGUISH A CLAIM FROM ITS DENIAL, and reflow2 leans on lexical matching in its catalogue, its search and its newest detector.

⭐⭐ AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE REAL FINDING, which is Anthony's point rather than this session's. A REFLOW2 DEVELOPER HAS A CRUTCH NO CONSUMER HAS. When the surface failed today it cost nothing, because the source was one grep away — so the failure never registered as a failure. A consumer agent on hxm_program or dev_storyflow has ONLY the served surface: it cannot grep reflow2's Rust, it would have called `plan_epoch`, and it would have had no second channel to discover the mistake. Every gap this project's own sessions route around by reading source is a WALL for the people the tool is for, and routing around it is precisely what stops it being found. `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` names the posture; this measures what happens when the posture slips.

📌 A SECOND MEASUREMENT, taken with it, showing the same thing from the description side: the rule that `record_change` REFUSES to record history into a `planned` epoch is real, enforced, and behaviour-changing. `record_change`'s served description mentions "planned" ZERO times. `add_epoch`'s mentions it zero times. So a consumer can only learn that invariant by being refused — the surface teaching by refusal rather than by description, which is the same defect fixed three times narrowly this week (`concern`'s values, `detected_at`'s absence, `suggested_depth`'s default) and never as a class.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED. One query is one data point; whether `find_tools` is broadly poor or badly served by this particular phrasing is unmeasured, and building a verdict on n=1 would be the error this project names elsewhere. What IS established without further measurement: the correct tool was absent from the top five, the ranked hit was its semantic opposite, and nobody would have noticed had the source not been to hand.
